- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to +2–3% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 1–2% buffer to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reverse direction: if price drops >5% from peak, forecast should trend down.
- Model overfits recent high volatility; apply smoothing: if 3 consecutive days show >5% price swing, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion trend.
- If multiple auction events in 7 days, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast sensitivity to supply events by 15–20%.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and model is trending, check for lag: if true outcome is 2–3 days behind, adjust forecast to lag by 1–2 days.
